title: Redwood Structured Output + Function Calling Demo - NovaTech
summary: Demo focused on Redwood's structured JSON output and function/tool-calling features (JSON mode, schemas, guardrails). Covered API examples, Console walkthrough, Optimize recommendations for batching and quantization, and security controls for Private/Dedicated deployments. Agreed on pilot and follow-ups: security docs, sample payloads, pilot kickoff week of 2026-02-23.
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-02-14
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Daniel Park (NovaTech Head of Platform), Meera Shah (NovaTech Security Lead), Luis Ortega (NovaTech ML Engineer)

Summary: quick demo of Redwood JSON-mode structured output + function calling and how to enforce schemas/guardrails, and a short Console tour for routes and Optimize recommendations.

00:00 Alex Kim: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, we're excited to show a couple things today — structured output, function/tool calling in JSON mode, and a bit of the Console and Optimize tips. can everyone see my screen?
00:12 Daniel Park: yes we can, looks good. thanks Alex.
00:18 Priya Rao: cool, I'll take you through a quick end-to-end where we define a schema for invoice parsing and then call a mock enrichment tool to attach vendor data. you'll see how Redwood's guardrails keep the output constrained.
00:33 Meera Shah: quick ask up front — we need to validate data residency and KMS integration for any PII we might send; that will affect whether we can use hosted or need dedicated/private.
00:44 Alex Kim: totally, Meera. we'll note the security docs and the KMS options. we support customer-managed keys in Private and Dedicated modes, and we have SOC2 audit artifacts we can share.
00:58 Priya Rao: ok jumping in — here's the API demo. request body in JSON mode, we pass a schema definition in the call params, you can see the schema expects fields invoice_number, total_amount (number), vendor {name, tax_id}, and line_items array. the model is instructed to only return strict JSON that validates against the schema.
01:20 Luis Ortega: sorry to interrupt — when you say schema, is that JSON Schema v4 or v7-ish? how strict is the validation?
01:27 Priya Rao: good q. we currently support a subset similar to JSON Schema draft-07 for types and required fields; we also validate shapes server-side and can apply post-generation validators. if the model output doesn't validate we either return a structured error or trigger a fallback policy.
01:45 Daniel Park: and that fallback — can it call a sanitization function or re-run the model?
01:50 Priya Rao: yes, you can configure automatic retries, a deterministic sanitizer function, or route to a lower-capacity model for cheaper attempts. also you can register a tool/function that transforms the raw output and returns validated JSON.
02:05 Alex Kim: show them the function call flow please.
02:08 Priya Rao: sure — in Console I'm clicking into the route config. here we attach a schema and link a tool endpoint: one we use for vendor enrichment, which takes vendor tax_id and returns canonical vendor info from NovaTech's vendor DB. this tool is represented as a callable function in the runtime.
02:29 Meera Shah: is that function executed in our network or Redwood's?
02:33 Priya Rao: depends on deployment. Hosted can call an HTTPS webhook you provide; in Private or Dedicated we can configure callbacks over VPC peering or private connectors so the function invocation stays within your network.
02:45 Luis Ortega: latency-wise, how much overhead does tool calling add? if every invoice requires a vendor lookup that could be hundreds of calls.
02:52 Priya Rao: good point — performance depends on batching and async options. Redwood supports batching of tool calls and async callbacks: the model can emit a batch of lookups which the runtime will call in parallel. Optimize suggests batching configs based on observed sequences to minimize overall token and wall-time cost.
03:08 Daniel Park: can you show an actual run?
03:11 Priya Rao: yes. running a sample prompt — "Extract invoice fields from this text" — and here's the returned payload. timestamp: 03:22 — output shows strict JSON, and the runtime validated it against schema. now the tool call trigger field vendor.tax_id is present, so Redwood invoked the registered vendor_enrich endpoint.
03:34 (console shows request log)
03:36 Alex Kim: note the log line — token counts, latency, and a per-route breakdown. that's what powers the Optimize recommendations.
03:45 Meera Shah: about logs — what's retained and who can see them? SSO, RBAC?
03:50 Alex Kim: Console has RBAC and audit logs. you can limit access to the raw transcripts, and logs can be configured to redact or not store PII. retention is configurable per account; we'll share the security docs.
04:05 Priya Rao: back to the demo — the vendor_enrich returned a canonical vendor object, Redwood merged it into the validated JSON and returned final output. if the enrichment endpoint had errored, our fallback flow would attach an enrichment_error and optionally call a different service.
04:25 Luis Ortega: what about guardrails for hallucinations — like if the model invents a tax ID?
04:31 Priya Rao: two-pronged: schema enforces types/formatting, and we also run a post-generation validator which can check checksums, length, regex for tax IDs. for high-assurance flows you can require verification against an external authority via tool call before accepting the record.
04:48 Daniel Park: and how do we handle partial extractions — say a line item amount is missing?
04:52 Priya Rao: we surface a partial response with a validation_errors array. you can configure the route to: a) return partial with errors, b) reject and retry, or c) queue for human review.
05:08 Meera Shah: what about encryption at rest? we need CMEK via our cloud KMS.
05:12 Alex Kim: supported in Dedicated and Private; hosted has platform-managed keys by default but we offer bring-your-own-key for higher tiers. we'll include KMS integration notes in the follow-up.
05:25 (30-second demo showing SDK code snippet)
05:26 Priya Rao: here's a Python SDK call that sets mode: "json_schema": { ... } and function_call: { "name": "vendor_enrich", "endpoint": "https://internal.novatech.com/enrich" }
05:49 Priya Rao: note the mode parameter — it flips the runtime to strict JSON generation and validation path. also you can attach pre-defined schema packs in Console so devs don't paste big schemas in every request.
06:05 Luis Ortega: any guardrails for cost? we have millions of invoices, want to avoid 10x cost per invoice.
06:12 Alex Kim: Optimize suggestions help here. for high-volume parsers we recommend: 1) prefix caching for common instruction templates, 2) quantized model variants for lower cost, 3) micro-batching of multiple invoices per request where acceptable, and 4) fallback to smaller model for lower-confidence pages. we'll run a cost projection during the pilot.
06:30 Daniel Park: curious about telemetry — can we see per-customer token breakdown and per-route SLO violations?
06:36 Alex Kim: yep, Console shows token-level breakdowns, per-route 95th/99th latency, error traces, and links to raw transcripts. you can also export metrics to your observability stack.
06:48 Priya Rao: jumping to the Optimize tab — here we have suggested batching windows, suggested quantization levels based on your sequence length distribution. for example, if average sequence length is under 128 tokens we recommend an int8 quantized variant.
07:05 Meera Shah: any regressions risk with quantization? quality monitoring?
07:10 Priya Rao: yes we recommend an eval suite. Redwood integrates evals so you can run regression tests against a labeled prompt set; alerts trigger if quality metrics drop. you can then pin a model version in the route or abort a rollout.
07:27 (short silence while demo loads)
07:32 Daniel Park: ok this is good. a couple practical items — can we get a sample request/response log for our team to replicate? also we need the security pack.
07:40 Alex Kim: absolutely, we'll share a demo notebook, sample logs, and the security whitepaper.
07:45 Luis Ortega: for the pilot, we'd like to test both hosted and Dedicated to compare latency and cost; can you help us design the benchmark?
07:53 Priya Rao: yes — we'll propose a benchmark plan with sample dataset size, 95/99 latency targets, and cost projection.
08:00 Meera Shah: timeline — we're looking to decide in the next 3–4 weeks, pilot start ideally week of 2/23.
08:07 Alex Kim: sounds reasonable. next steps we'll share artifacts and schedule a pilot kickoff.

28:00 (mid-call — deeper Q&A about error cases, more console clicking and logs)

40:12 Alex Kim: quick recap: 1) Send security pack and SOC2 — Alex will own; 2) Demo notebook + sample schema examples — Priya will own; 3) NovaTech to share sample invoice dataset and priority success criteria — Daniel/Luis will own; 4) Schedule pilot kickoff for week of 2026-02-23.
40:40 Meera Shah: noted. can you also include scoping doc for Dedicated capacity and rough pricing?
40:47 Alex Kim: yes, will include Dedicated pricing and a hosted vs dedicated TCO comparison.
40:54 Daniel Park: thanks all, this was helpful.
40:58 Alex Kim: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts in the next 48–72 hours.
41:10 (call ends)

Priya Rao: Share demo notebook, sample request/response logs, and schema examples by 2026-02-16
Daniel Park / Luis Ortega: Provide sample invoice dataset and success criteria by 2026-02-20
Priya Rao: Draft benchmark plan (latency/cost) for hosted vs Dedicated by 2026-02-18
